result.killer: None found. Partial overlaps: goAML registration is free and one-off (FSJ). FinStat AML covers PEP, sanctions and beneficial-owner screening. AKMV sells law-firm AML document packs.
result.reason: I found nothing that kills it. I found no Slovak SaaS that bundles the internal AML programme (§20), client checks and beneficial-owner records, risk scoring and the annual training log for real estate agencies, accountants or tax advisers. No templates or tools from the chambers or associations turned up (NARKS, SKDP), though I did not check their member areas. Partial overlaps: goAML registration is free and one-off, so it has little paid value. FinStat AML covers beneficial-owner, PEP and sanctions screening; its price was not found and its page returned 403. Law-firm packs (AKMV, from EUR 600) cover the programme document. UK tools such as AMLHUB and AMLCheck are not adapted to Slovak law. Pravne noviny says only 'thousands of firms and sole traders' are affected, without a count. Sole-trader accountants are likely to pay little. After 30 Nov the recurring core is client checks, records and programme updates. I score it below the first check.

Existing duties only: monthly distributor report to the customs office (excise act 98/2004), biofuel quantity report to the Ministry of Economy (act 309/2009), weekly statistical return for retail fuel, and a verified dispensing-pump rule. The Czech fuel-station register does not apply in Slovakia. The SITA piece 'Predajcov pohonných látok čakajú nové povinnosti' had no date in the snippet, so it is unverified. No candidate.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: No search spent: the budget went to categories where a 2026-27 trigger appeared. Related lead: timber and forest records, see 32.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Searched only owners' associations (SVB) and property managers, covered under 31. No 2026 trigger found. Housing and agricultural co-operatives and credit unions were not searched.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Found vyhláška 113/2026 on staffing and equipment of ambulances (from 1 July 2026), vyhláška 236/2025, and the eHealth mandatory-connection debate. Clinic software and the eKasa cash-register duty already exist. No clear gap. Weak candidate recorded.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Precursor permission and suspicious-order reporting (act 331/2005, EU 273/2004) are old rules, with SÚKL guidance MP 123/2021. No new 2026 duty found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Strong lead: a draft amendment of act 5/2004 (proposed effective 1 Jan 2027) would make temporary-work agencies report every assignment electronically to the Labour Office, with fines up to EUR 100,000 and tax and levy proof for user employers. It is a draft only (article dated 1 Sep 2026), so it is unverified. The existing duty is the 7-working-day notice for third-country nationals (Príloha 13). Security and cleaning agencies were not searched.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: The new building act 60/2025 and Portál výstavby give site managers, supervisors and contractors their own access, and the diary is part of the system. Whether the electronic diary is mandatory for contractors was not confirmed. Related to K03 but a different buyer. Recorded as unverified. Mining and quarries not searched.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Strong lead: AML act 297/2008 amended by act 73/2026 (in force 1 Jun 2026, parts 10 Jul 2026). All existing obliged persons (real estate agencies, accountants with a trade licence, tax advisers, auditors) must register in goAML by 30 Nov 2026. Beneficial-owner checks against reliable sources now apply. FSJ plans full on-site inspections of real estate agencies in 2026, and fines reach EUR 1m. Only lawyers' document packs (AKMV, from EUR 600) found as competitors; no KYC or AML app found.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Guest registers are known (K08, K12). New: act 133/2026 sets up a register of short-term rental units, effective 1 Jan 2027. Every unit offered on a platform needs a registration number, and existing hosts must register by 28 Feb 2027. Fines are EUR 100-1,000 for individuals, EUR 1,000-3,000 for traders and legal entities, and EUR 3,000-30,000 for platforms. See candidate.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: EUDR for wood is known (K09). The food-exporter search found nothing relevant. Found timber-origin rules (decree 204/2024, in force 1 Jun 2025) and forest records decree 120/2025 (1 Jan 2026), recorded under 32. Fish not searched.

coverage.category: 31. Owners' associations (SVB) and housing property managers (country-specific)
coverage.found: Act 182/1993 was amended by 325/2024 (from 1 Jan 2025: electronic voting, more transparency on debtors). Managers' register is under act 246/2015. No 2026-27 trigger found. Competing management software was not checked.

coverage.category: 32. Forest owners, urbár and land communities, sawmills and timber traders (country-specific)
coverage.found: Decree 204/2024 (marking of harvested timber and origin documents, from 1 Jun 2025) and decree 120/2025 (forest records, from 1 Jan 2026) changed the paperwork. The forest act amendment tightened reporting of accidental felling. Details and software not confirmed.

coverage.category: 33. Packaging and producer-responsibility registrants (country-specific)
coverage.found: Producers register in the register of producers of reserved products and file an annual packaging report with their Príloha 17 filing (decree 366/2015). They can use a producer-responsibility organisation (OZV), which usually does the filing. The PPWR starts applying 12 Aug 2026 (unverified detail). Thresholds for small producers not found.

coverage.category: 34. Private social-service providers (care homes, home-care agencies) (country-specific)
coverage.found: Non-public providers file an annual report to the accounts register by 15 July (act 448/2008, § 67a). MPSVR plans an amendment effective 31 Dec 2026, only a presentation, not enacted. No concrete new duty.

coverage.category: 35. Short-term rental hosts and platform-linked letting (act 133/2026) (country-specific)
coverage.found: See 29 and the candidate. The registration is by the host in the ministry's e-service. The text mentions no representative or API for third parties.

coverage.category: 36. Electronic construction records on Portál výstavby for site managers and contractors (country-specific)
coverage.found: See 27. A 2023 press report says traders keep construction documentation only in the system from 1 Apr 2024 and individuals from 2028. This was not re-verified against act 60/2025 and its decrees.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: The main 2026 change is the new Act 384/2025 on sales records (eKasa), in force 1 Jan 2026. It covers nearly all sellers, market and ambulant sellers included; cashless acceptance for sales over EUR 1 was moved to 1 May 2026 per one source (the fiscal-requirements.com article says 1 March). Penalties run EUR 1,500-20,000, and EUR 3,000-40,000 for repeat breaches. The state offers a virtual cash register and online/software registers, so this is a generic POS duty and a free state tool exists. Market operators (e.g. Rajec) ask sellers for an ORP/SORP code or a declaration of exemption. No market-operator or stall-management software found (the one search returned only noise). Direct farm sales (predaj z dvora) fall under Govt. Regs 359/2011 and 360/2011 with registration at the RVPS; no 2026 change or software found. Money changers: licence from NBS under Act 202/1995 plus a trade licence; NBS Decree 139/2013 amended by 375/2025 (in force 1 Jan 2026); no sign of repeal or a new law; the number of licensed offices and the NBS register were not found, and the segment is likely tiny. No candidate beyond the weak ones below.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: The only quiet-sector duty found is the food-security stock notification under s.24 of Act 152/1995, filed through a ministry e-form (annexes 3-5 of Decree 258/2022). The decree was valid 21 Jul 2022 to 31 Dec 2025, and no successor was found. A 2024 consultation recorded business asking for the duty to be dropped. The obliged group and thresholds (annexes 1-2) could not be read, so this stays unverified. Feed businesses register with ÚKSÚP under Act 271/2005 (no 2026 change found). No grain-buyer or mill register, and no purpose-built grain-intake software (only an old Q-SHR warehouse program in a CRZ contract). Intervention-storage contracts with PPA exist but are optional. Related wood-trade lead (cat. 30/32): Act 113/2018 (traders keep proof of wood acquisition and trade right; transport documents kept 5 years) shows as repealed by Act 81/2025 (EU deforestation implementation), with the repeal date unclear (slov-lex shows a 29.12.2026 version; zakonypreludi shows 2025 versions). This is the same EUDR area as K09. Coffee and cocoa: nothing country-specific found.

result.competitor: Free state tool: the ÚPSVR/MPSVR portal poskytovatel.gov.sk already has 'Pracovné vzťahy s agentúrou' and 'Dočasné pridelenia' sections for ADZ, with manual entry, Excel export and a bulk JSON import against published JSON schemas (manuals 'Evidovanie údajov ADZ' and 'Import dát ADZ', 14 Nov 2025). Commercial: Humanet payroll/HR has an agency-employment module covering orders, timesheets, wages and invoicing (article from 2015; not checked whether it exports to the portal). No dedicated reporting middleware found, but the state's JSON import makes this an easy add-on for existing vendors.
result.duty: Draft amendment from the Labour Ministry, not in force as of Sep 2026 (proposed effective date 1 Jan 2027): each temporary assignment would be reported electronically to ÚPSVR one day before it starts, its end no earlier than the next working day, other changes within 10 working days (now 30 calendar days), fines up to 100,000 EUR. Bill number and passage status not found (slov-lex search gave nothing). Agencies already record employment relations and assignments in the ÚPSVR portal poskytovatel.gov.sk and file annual reports electronically.
result.market: 441 temporary work agencies operating in Slovakia, down from more than 600 (Labour Ministry, 28 May 2026). The public register is kept by ÚPSVR. The split by agency size was not checked.
result.reason: The duty is only a draft. Pravnenoviny (1 Sep 2026) says the per-assignment e-reporting rule ("nič z toho ešte neplatí") would start 1 Jan 2027, with fines up to 100,000 EUR. No bill number or slov-lex record turned up. The core job already has a free state tool. ÚPSVR's portal poskytovatel.gov.sk has a "Dočasné pridelenia" section for ADZ, with manual entry, Excel export and bulk JSON import against published schemas (manuals dated 14 Nov 2025). The draft mainly shortens deadlines inside a reporting channel that already exists, and HR or payroll vendors such as Humanet (agency module) can add a JSON export. The market is tiny: 441 agencies (Ministry, May 2026). That leaves little room beyond a converter feature.

result.competitor: goAML registration itself is a free FSJ portal with an FSJ user manual, so the one-off registration step has little paid value. Law-firm document packs exist, e.g. AKMV's AML documentation for real estate agencies (claim says from EUR 600; not re-checked). FinStat sells AML services to obliged persons, with PEP-database checks via portal or API, which partly covers screening. International KYC vendors (Sumsub, with a Slovak page) do ID, PEP and sanctions checks. No Slovak SaaS was found that bundles the internal AML programme, client checks and beneficial-owner records, risk scoring and report preparation for small agencies or accountants. Searches for KROS or other accounting-software AML modules found nothing (not confirmed absent). Chamber or association tools (NARKS, SKDP, SKAU) were not checked.
result.duty: Confirmed under Slovak law. Act 297/2008 Z.z., as amended by Act 73/2026 Z.z., has been in force since 1 Jun 2026 (some parts from 10 Jul 2026). The obliged persons named include accountants with a bookkeeping trade licence (not in-house employees), tax advisers, auditors and real estate agencies. Notaries and lawyers are obliged only for certain activities. Existing obliged persons must register in goAML by 30 Nov 2026 (§36d); new ones have 30 days. Registration is electronic only and needs a registration form, a business authorisation document and a named administrator. Podnikajte says failing to register is an administrative offence with a fine up to EUR 1m. Pravnenoviny speaks only of fines in the hundreds of thousands of euros for the gravest breaches. Unusual-transaction reports have been filed only through goAML since 2025. Ongoing duties: beneficial-owner and ownership checks from several reliable sources (now for all clients), a written internal AML programme (§20(2)) with a named responsible person, and PEP and sanctions checks (§10(1)(d)). FSJ inspections often find missing or outdated programmes.
result.market: Not verified. Pravnenoviny says only that "thousands" of firms and sole traders are affected. Neither register counts (bookkeeping licences, real-estate brokers) nor FSJ sector statistics were reached; the FSJ 2025 annual report PDF could not be parsed. A partial decode of the FSJ 2026 inspection plan (PKC2026) suggests only about 3 real estate agencies are planned for checks (uncertain), plus off-site AML questionnaires. The LinkedIn figures (223 agencies, EUR 142k fines) remain unverified.
result.reason: The duty is real. Act 73/2026 amends Act 297/2008 and has been in force since 1 Jun 2026. Existing obliged persons must register in goAML by 30 Nov 2026. Podnikajte says a missed registration can draw a fine up to EUR 1m. Beneficial-owner checks against several sources now apply to all clients. Unusual-transaction reports have gone only through goAML since 2025. Registration itself is free and fast, so the paid job is the ongoing work: the internal AML programme, KYC and beneficial-owner records. Only partial competitors turned up: law-firm packs (AKMV), FinStat's PEP/AML screening, and Sumsub. No Slovak SME AML workflow app was found. Enforcement looks light (the 2026 plan possibly covers only 3 agencies, on a partly decoded read). The deadline peak fades after November, and the market size was not checked.

result.competitor: No dedicated software or done-for-you registration service found in Slovak searches. AKMV, a law firm, sells consultations on the register for EUR 130. The state e-service is free and needs only a simple form: address, land-registry data, beds, host identity. Platforms are legally required to block listings without a number, so Airbnb and Booking will almost certainly add a registration-number field, as they have in other EU countries. Not checked: whether PMS or channel-manager vendors such as Previo will add one, and whether Slovakia's general electronic-mandate rules would let agents file for hosts.
result.duty: Act 133/2026 Z. z. (Slovakia, published 18 June 2026, in force 1 Jan 2027; implements EU 2024/1028) is real. Hosts renting short-term through online platforms register each unit with the Ministry of Tourism and Sport before the first listing (§5(1)). Hosts already renting have until 28 Feb 2027 (§14). Changes are due within 30 days and deletion within 30 days of stopping (§5(4), §5(7)). Registration is free (§5(10)). It is done through the register's e-service form, authorized under the e-Government Act, or in person for individuals (§5(5)-(6)). If defects aren't fixed, the number is suspended and then revoked (§6). Fines: individuals EUR 100-1,000 (§10); traders and companies EUR 1,000-3,000; platforms EUR 3,000-30,000; repeats up to double (§11). The law names no proxy, third-party agent or API. Platforms file through the e-service but get no access to the register. Accommodation-tax administrators and tax authorities do get access (§7).
result.market: Not confirmed from a register. A nehnutelnosti.sk article cites estimates of about 10,000 accommodation providers. It also reports a hotel association (AHRS) claim that in some cities platform listings are up to four times the number of officially registered hosts. Most hosts appear to be private individuals with one or two units. The number of multi-unit managers is not quantified. The startitup article says only "thousands".
result.reason: The duty is real, mandatory and well documented, with real fines. But the core job is a one-off, free, simple e-form per unit. Changes and deletions after that are rare. Most hosts are private individuals with one unit and little reason to pay. The deadline creates some urgency until Feb 2027, then the need fades. Platforms must enforce the registration number, so they will build the field themselves. There is no API or proxy for third parties, which limits automation for managers. The best angle is to bundle it into existing guest-register or police-reporting and accommodation-tax tools (K08/K12) for multi-unit managers, not to sell it alone. The market is small (about 10k hosts).

Duty partly real: water act 364/2004 §6(5) (amended 2016, zákon 303/2016) already requires holders of a §21(1) groundwater permit to report abstraction data to a "poverená osoba". The VÚVH deck presents a 2026 amendment (annual report by 31 Jan, mandatory metering) as effective 1 Jan 2026. I could not read the PDF (binary) or find the final enacted text, the penalty, or who the poverená osoba is. The only 1 Jan 2026 item found on slov-lex was an unrelated government regulation. No competitor or state portal was found, but I did not find one searching only a few queries. The market count is not found. Reporting is annual and low-volume, so frequency and willingness to pay are weak. Narrow, state-run channel, hard to distribute.

result.duty: Periodic odborné prehliadky and skúšky of vyhradené technické zariadenia under vyhláška 508/2009 Z.z., with logbooks. Intervals and penalties not verified.
result.market: Not quantified. No register count found.
result.reason: The duty exists in outline. Vyhláška 508/2009 Z.z. covers tlakové, zdvíhacie, plynové and elektrické vyhradené technické zariadenia, with periodic odborné prehliadky and skúšky. Its last amendment found was 398/2013 (effective 2014-01-01). I could not confirm that the 2026 consolidated text is in force, nor the exact intervals or penalties. A lift contract cites 4x/year inspections, a 3-year expert test and a 6-year official test, which is contract text only. Competition exists: SunSoft.VTZ (dated .NET 2.0 desktop software) tracks VTZ and inspection deadlines, and tenders ask for harmonogram software. Revision firms usually handle the schedules themselves. The market is fragmented and I found no new 2025-27 trigger. Budget was used on 4 searches and 0 fetches, so market size was not checked. Pain and buyer accessibility are modest.

Duty is real: Act 131/2010 (version in force from 15 Jul 2026) requires funeral firms to keep a per-person handling register and an operating rulebook (submitted to the regional public health office), and requires cemetery operators to keep a cemetery register and photograph each dug grave. Fines run up to 663 EUR, administered mostly by municipalities. The 15 Jul 2026 change is not identified. The listing shows amendment 165/2026 mainly as a public-health act amendment, so it is probably not a new trigger. The duties are one-off or ongoing record keeping, not periodic filings. Competition exists: virtualnecintoriny.sk/3wsk.sk sell grave management to municipalities for hundreds of EUR, and a CRZ contract shows a web app for funeral-firm records. No firm count was found. Weak, small market.

The duty is real. Act 56/2012 §27 requires a 10-year concession, and each vehicle must be listed in the concession and the taxi register (§27(17)-(18)). §29 requires door marking, a TAXI roof sign and a copy of the concession in the vehicle. The 2024 amendment (162/2024) made the driver liable for marking. The 1 Apr 2027 version exists (amended by Act 131/2026), but I did not read what it changes (§56m cut off). Fine amounts for marking were not found. Existing software (Senset, Tiskel, Bolt dispatch) does dispatch, not compliance. The workflow is mostly one-off listing and a 15-day change notice, not a recurring one. Market size was not found. Weak recurring pain and low willingness to pay.

The duty is real but the "no competitor" gap fails. Act 25/2025 Z. z. (the building act; 60/2025 is only the decree) requires a construction diary kept by an authorised person (§ 6 ods. 5), "spravidla v elektronickej podobe" (§ 10 ods. 2). I could not read the fine provisions or the transitional dates. Several Slovak e-diary products already exist: Stavario and Buildary.online (KROS), estavebnydennik.sk, dennikstavby.sk and e-dennik.sk. The market is crowded and the diary is not mandated on the Portál. I did not find a business count. Wording is "generally electronic", not strictly mandatory.

The duty is real but mis-cited, and the filing is done by others on free state tools. Decree "204/2024" was not found. Timber marking and origin documents fall under decree 232/2006, amended by 120/2025 (in force 1 Jun 2025). Forest records decree 297/2011 was amended by 121/2025 (from 1 Jan 2026), not 120/2025. Records are kept electronically in the state forest information system (NLC ISLHP), a free state web application, or in software that submits to it. Accidental-felling reports go through the NLC portal, which only the professional forest manager (odborný lesný hospodár) can log into. So the filer is a professional, not the owner, and buyer access is poor. No commercial niche software was found, but the search was shallow and no market count was verified. This is a weak, unverified niche.

decisions.reason: New: small temp-work agencies, mandatory assignment e-reporting with a 1 Jan 2027 trigger.
New: associations above 35k EUR must file annual income/donor statements by 15 Jul; no known idea covers it.
